name: Anupam Rasayan India Ltd
title: Anupam Rasayan India Ltd - 543275 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Anupam FY26 consolidated revenue rose 65% to INR2,384 crores, with Q4 PAT of INR56 crores versus INR63 crores a year earlier.
summary.overview: FY26 was the highest revenue year for Anupam, with consolidated revenue from operations of INR2,384 crores (up 65% YoY) and EBITDA including other income of INR543 crores (23% margin). Q4 consolidated total income rose 26% YoY to INR639 crores, but EBITDA fell to INR141 crores from INR150 crores and PAT fell to INR56 crores from INR63 crores; Q4 includes Tanfac and only 1 month and 2 days of Jayhawk. Management announced a definitive agreement to acquire a 43.3% to 48.2% stake in Bliss GVS Pharma plus an open offer for up to 26%, and said the last leg of capex (INR315 crores) is complete with no major capex planned. Operating cash flow reached INR334 crores on working capital release.

financial_highlights.value: Agrochemicals 55%, Pharma 20%, Performance Materials 18%, Personal Care 7%

segments.name: Agrochemicals (standalone)
segments.commentary: 55% of standalone FY26 revenue, down from 76% in FY22. Management expects agro to continue recouping and growing.

segments.name: Pharma (standalone)
segments.commentary: 20% of FY26 revenue (INR339 crores), mainly KSM. Management expects it to grow faster than agro, with the Bliss acquisition adding a formulation platform.

segments.name: Performance Materials / Polymer
segments.commentary: 18% of FY26 standalone revenue (INR305 crores). Management expects higher growth from polymer, with new projects and the EV and Elementium contracts cited as drivers.

segments.name: Tanfac (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Fluorination platform securing hydrofluoric acid and potassium fluoride supply. Introducing new products and customers in FY27; pro forma revenue cited at INR711 crores.

segments.name: Jayhawk Fine Chemicals (US)
segments.commentary: Acquisition completed; pro forma annual revenue about US$76 million (about INR722 crores). Only 1 month and 2 days consolidated in FY26.

guidance_outlook: Standalone revenue growth of 20% to 30% CAGR over the next 3 to 5 years is the target, after 60% to 70% growth in FY26.
Blended EBITDA margins expected to stay near FY26 levels (about 24% standalone, per Q&A); management sees upward bias from pharma and polymer but declined to guide until products ramp up.
Standalone tax rate expected to be around 25% going forward.
Working capital expected to keep improving in FY27; pro forma consolidated working capital about 215 to 220 days, and about 240 to 250 days excluding Jayhawk.

Bliss GVS synergies expected to show in CDMO projects within 6 to 12 months, with more by 18 months. Deal expected to be EPS accretive from day 1; closing timeline 2 to 3 months, subject to SEBI approval and open offer.
Pro forma group revenue above INR4,000 crores and consolidated EBITDA about INR834 crores (Anupam INR1,676 crores, Tanfac INR711 crores, Jayhawk about INR722 crores, Bliss INR927 crores).
capex_capacity: FY26 capex of INR315 crores completed the last leg of the capex programme; all plants are now commercialised.
No major capex is planned as current capacity covers near-term growth. Standalone maintenance capex guided at INR50 to 75 crores (including efficiency programmes).
Standalone gross block of about INR2,500 to 2,600 crores; management sees potential to support about INR3,500 crores of revenue from this block.
Bliss GVS currently runs at about 30% utilisation on revenue of about INR1,000 crores; management targets 60% to 70%.
Separate Halol capex of about INR250 crores for a CDMO project from a large multinational pharma customer; management expects asset turnover of 4x to 5x and gave no detailed timeline.
demand_pricing: Order book is about INR14,000 crores. Management estimates INR1,700 to 1,800 crores of annual incremental revenue from the pipeline on a 6 to 7 year average basis, partly agro and partly polymer.
Pharma growth is expected from Indian organic demand on a standalone basis; Jayhawk and Bliss synergies are additional.
Jayhawk shares some common customers with Anupam, and there are complementary customers; Bliss has overlap on the CDMO side.
Anupam has no African exposure; Bliss has meaningful Africa exposure, per management's comments.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for the Bliss GVS acquisition and whether current management will continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management continues. Bliss runs at about 30% utilisation and could reach 60% to 70%. The deal adds a full pharma platform from KSM to finished dosage. Tanfac will remain a separate entity.

qa_highlights.question: Pro forma revenue, merger or delisting plans, synergies, funding and EPS impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Pro forma group revenue above INR4,000 crores and EBITDA about INR834 crores. No merger or delisting planned. Funding is about INR300 crores of NCDs in a wholly owned subsidiary, with the balance as non-controlling, non-voting quasi-equity. Deal to be EPS accretive from day 1.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone growth trajectory and business mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone grew over 60% to 70% this year. Management targets 20% to 30% CAGR over 3 to 5 years, led by pharma and polymer with agro also growing.

qa_highlights.question: Debt levels and interest cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated gross debt about INR1,500 crores, net about INR1,100 crores; over two-thirds is working capital loans. Adding INR300 crores gives net debt of about INR1,400 to 1,500 crores against EBITDA above INR650 crores on the stated basis. Interest cost not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Gross block capacity, maintenance capex and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross block can support about INR3,500 crores of revenue. Maintenance capex INR50 to 75 crores. Blended margins guided to stay near FY26 levels, with upward bias from pharma and polymer.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Bliss promoter sell and what is the structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited succession planning by the senior promoter, who wants cash for his family. The promoter chose Anupam over other offers. Stake range 43.3% to 48.2% lets the seller keep about 5%.

risks_watch: Q4 EBITDA and PAT declined YoY despite higher revenue; Q4 includes only 1 month and 2 days of Jayhawk.
Debt rising to about INR1,400 to 1,500 crores net on a pro forma basis with the INR300 crores NCD; interest cost not disclosed.
Bliss deal subject to SEBI approval and open offer results; management declined to answer several questions on Bliss until the deal closes.
Possible customer conflict as Anupam moves into regulated pharma formulations (CDMO and finished dosage), per analyst question.
Management stated it will not guide on margins for ramping pharma and polymer products.
Standalone tax rate guided down to about 25%, which supports PAT.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and strategy, with specific targets for 20% to 30% CAGR. Cautious and deliberately evasive on Bliss GVS specifics (CDMO scope, Africa exposure, management interaction) until the transaction closes.
key_quotes: FY '26 has been a landmark year for Anupam Rasayan as we delivered our highest ever revenue.
Consequently, our dependence on agrochemicals has reduced from 76% revenue contribution in FY '22 to 55% in FY '26.
We are not envisaging any major capex in near future as current capacity is enough to take care of the near-term growth.
Yes, we are envisaging a lower tax rate going forward. I think going forward, we should be looking at around about 25% as a tax rate going forward.

adds.what: Separate Halol CDMO plant for large multinational pharma customer (capex ~INR250 crore, no detailed timeline given)

growth.why: Management guides standalone revenue CAGR of 20-30% over 3-5 years (midpoint ~25%) after 60-70% growth in FY26, backed by a INR14,000 crore order book and INR1,700-1,800 crore estimated annual incremental pipeline revenue, though no major capex is planned and the Halol CDMO project has no timeline.
